subject: [PATCH 8/8] mm/gup: batch contiguous same-folio PTEs into one refcount grab

2026-11-02.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the handling of large folios in the Linux kernel's memory management system by batching contiguous PTEs into a single refcount grab, reducing overhead and improving performance. The patch introduces a new function `gup_pte_batch_len` to determine how many PTEs can be committed as one run, and modifies the `gup_grab_folio_pages` function to take advantage of this optimization. This results in significant performance improvements for large folios, with a 12.8x reduction in execution time for 64 kB mTHP mappings.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) noted that the patch needs more work and suggested basing it on top of the gup-fast series, which provides helpers for checking required unsharing of multiple PTEs.
reviews.raw_body:
That's a clear indication that this needs more work.

I'll try to get to it soon and see how it could be done in a cleaner way, likely
it should be based on top of the gup-fast series where we will have helpers to
check for required unsharing of multiple PTEs.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author is addressing a concern about the sequence of merging helper functions, offering two options for combining the series and suggests getting rid of redundant code in gup.c
reviews.raw_body:
I'm all for sharing the same helpers.

How would you like to sequence things?

Do you prefer to merge both series separately,
and then get a follow-up series that merges
the helper functions?

Would you like Yeoreum Yun and me to combine
the series, merge the helper functions beforehand,
and then send you one larger, combined series?

I have spent enough time in gup.c that I would
be happy to get rid of some more of that code.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) confirmed that they plan to review the gup-fast series first and then build on top of it, indicating no immediate concerns or issues with the current patch.
reviews.raw_body:
My plan is to get the small series for gup-fast ready, stage that, and then
build on top of it.

By then I should have been able to dig through most of your series. The cleanups
can stay part of this series.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the patch may not work correctly for large folios and agreed to restructure in v2, indicating a fix is needed.

Author agrees to fold in a suggested cleanup and is open to sending it as a separate series or incorporating it into their existing patch set, but expresses uncertainty about the PUD and PMD paths.
reviews.raw_body:
On Tue, 3 Nov 2026 17:55:31 +0100
"David Hildenbrand (Arm)" <david@kernel.org> wrote:

---

That sounds good. It looks like with this small change below,
GUP-fast and slow GUP can share another helper.

I can fold that into my series as well, or send the cleanups
in a separate series, whatever works best for you.

The PUD and PMD paths do not look as easy to untangle, but
maybe after some more cleanups on each end?

---8<---

diff --git a/mm/gup.c b/mm/gup.c
--- a/mm/gup.c
+++ b/mm/gup.c
@@ -940,14 +940,20 @@
  * run under FOLL_WRITE or FOLL_PIN does need the per-page check, so it stays
  * one page at a time.
+ *
+ * @fpb_flags selects the scan: slow GUP merges young/dirty so
+ * folio_mark_dirty() sees any dirty PTE in the run; fast GUP scans
+ * locklessly and revalidates the run after grabbing it. @vma is only
+ * needed for FPB_MERGE_WRITE and may be NULL otherwise.
  */
 static unsigned long gup_pte_batch_len(struct vm_area_struct *vma,
 		unsigned long address, unsigned long walk_end,
-		struct folio *folio, pte_t *ptep, pte_t *batch_pte, unsigned int flags)
+		struct folio *folio, pte_t *ptep, pte_t *batch_pte,
+		unsigned int flags, fpb_t fpb_flags)
 {
 	unsigned long max;
@@ -961,8 +961,7 @@
 	max = (walk_end - address) >> PAGE_SHIFT;
 	if (max <= 1)
 		return 1;
 
-	/* Merge young/dirty across batch so folio_mark_dirty sees any dirty. */
 	return folio_pte_batch_flags(folio, vma, ptep, batch_pte, max,
-				     FPB_RESPECT_WRITE | FPB_MERGE_YOUNG_DIRTY);
+				     fpb_flags);
 }
@@ -1018,7 +1018,8 @@
 			folio = page_folio(page);
 			batch_pte = pte;
 
 			batch = gup_pte_batch_len(vma, address, walk_end, folio,
-					 ptep, &batch_pte, flags);
+					 ptep, &batch_pte, flags,
+					 FPB_RESPECT_WRITE | FPB_MERGE_YOUNG_DIRTY);
 			ret = gup_grab_folio_pages(folio, page, batch,
 						     pte_dirty(batch_pte), flags,

2026-11-03.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the handling of large folios in the Linux kernel's memory management system by batching contiguous PTEs into a single refcount grab, reducing overhead and improving performance for certain workloads. The patch introduces a new function `gup_pte_batch_len` to determine how many PTEs can be batched together, and modifies the `gup_grab_folio_pages` function to use this information. This change is particularly beneficial for large folios (mTHP) and reduces the number of refcount grabs required, leading to significant performance improvements.
